text:
anya: quick triage thread for sparkplug-v2-int6 onboarding. ran the full similarity+clustering battery on en/fr/de holdouts and got a notable degradation in cluster compactness and recall. anyone free to eyeball? :mag:

mike: drop the topline numbers and the quantization/calib details please.

anya: short summary below (abbreviated):

```
model: sparkplug-v2-int6
quant: per-channel symmetric, 6-bit
calibration: 1000 random pooled examples (en/fr/de)
whitening: enabled (sparsity-aware)
batching: micro=8
metrics (v1 -> v2):
  recall@1: 0.71 -> 0.68
  recall@5: 0.88 -> 0.84
  silhouette: 0.24 -> 0.15
  idflip_rate: 0.4% -> 3.2%
```

siva: idflip rising that much screams calibration bias. can you compute per-cluster centroid L2 deltas between v1 and v2? also per-channel scale ratios.

anya: did both. highlights:
- centroid_l2_delta median: 0.10, 90p: 0.28
- a few clusters (notably cluster 37 in DE longtail) ~0.6
- channels with big scale ratio: [12, 47, 203]
  channel 47 old_scale=0.0032 new_scale=0.0011 (ratio ~2.9)
  channel 203 old_scale=0.0007 new_scale=0.0023 (ratio ~0.3)

lina: that pattern is consistent with under-represented activation modes in the calibration sample. rare-token channels get noisy scale estimates -> harsher quantization error.

siva: do a stratified recalibration: ensure calibration sample includes token-frequency deciles and language splits. and run a unit-norm (cosine) eval to separate magnitude vs angular distortion.

anya: kicked off two follow-ups: (A) stratified-calib n=2000 (lang-split 50/25/25) (B) post-embedding L2 normalize run.

eval-bot: run queued 1769502468 -> full results + per-cluster nn histograms will post when done.

mike: also collect k=100 neighbor distance distributions intra vs inter and the silhouette per-cluster; helps confirm whether intra-cluster variance increased or inter-cluster gap shrank.

anya: micro-results after stratified recalib (small holdout ~2k each): recall@5 +1.1 pts, silhouette median +0.05, idflip -> 1.0%. centroid L2 median down to 0.06. still a handful of tail clusters >0.4 delta.

lina: good sign. can you upload the per-channel histograms (old vs stratified) and flag channels where scale ratio outside [0.5,2.0]? looks like those correlate with the problematic clusters.

anya: uploaded table to the eval report link (internal). short excerpt: channels flagged [12,47,203]. hypothesis: calibration pool randomness let a few high-frequency tokens dominate channel 47; stratified sampling reduces that effect. channel 203 had too few activations -> scale under-estimated previously.

siva: possible mitigations: (1) default stratified calibration for embedding quantization (with fallback to random when pool < threshold), (2) add tiny asymmetric quant option for channels with very low activation magnitudes, (3) CI test that synthesizes longtail queries to catch regressions.

mike: also try an asymmetric per-channel quant for the flagged channels only and see if it recovers the outliers without changing global behavior. if so, it's a pragmatic short-term patch.

anya: unit-norm micro-run shows partial recovery (~0.6-0.8 pts recall@5) but silhouette still lags on some tail clusters -> both norm shift and angular distortion contribute.

anya: immediate plan posted here: 1) finish full stratified recalib on full holdouts + k=100 nn histograms, 2) run selective asymmetric-per-channel experiment for flagged channels, 3) if stratified consistently helps, open PR to make stratified sampling the default for embedding calib and add a synthetic longtail integration test, 4) if asymmetric helps, include it behind a flag and add targeted unit tests. will loop in siva/lina on the per-channel tuning.

mike: sounds good. please paste the PR(s) here when opened. thx.

anya: will update in ~45m when full runs finish. :coffee:
